## Best 2kWh portable power station for an RV under $900

**My pick: BLUETTI AC200L — $899 (or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF).**

Based on your nine provided pages, it's the strongest overall choice for RV use because it combines a true 2kWh LiFePO4 battery, a built-in 30A RV outlet, high solar input, and a powerful inverter within your budget.

<AsyncImageGroup query={["BLUETTI AC200L portable power station front view TT-30 RV outlet","BLUETTI AC200L portable power station RV camping setup"]} aspectRatio="5:4" layout="bento"/>

### Top contenders compared

| Model | Capacity | AC output | RV outlet | Weight | Price |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|
| **BLUETTI AC200L** | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | TT-30 | 62.4 lb | **$899** |
| Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | TT-30 | 51 lb | $676.16 |
| OUPES Mega 2 Pro | 2,048Wh | 2,500W | TT-30 | 48.8 lb | $699 |
| Dabbsson DBS2100 Pro | 2,150Wh | 2,400W | RV outlet | 54 lb | $799 |
| Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 | ~2,000Wh | — | RV suitability | 41.7 lb | $899.99 |
| FOSSiBOT F2400 | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | — | — | $629 |

Sources: [DealElectric comparison](https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv), [GearRanking RV rankings](https://www.gearranking.com/power-stations/rv/), [Outage Ready Guide](https://outagereadyguide.com/2kwh-power-stations).

## Why I'd choose the BLUETTI AC200L

<AsyncImage query="BLUETTI AC200L portable power station product photo" aspectRatio="4:3"/>

- **RV-ready:** Built-in TT-30 outlet lets you plug in your RV shore-power cord directly.
- **Good inverter power:** 2,400W handles refrigerators, microwaves, coffee makers, and everyday RV essentials.
- **Excellent solar capability:** Up to 1,200W solar input, the highest among the models in the DealElectric comparison.
- **Expandable ecosystem:** Can integrate with additional BLUETTI equipment and charging accessories.
- **Competitive sale price:** The reported $854.05 coupon price makes it especially attractive.

Buy: [BLUETTI AC200L deal link](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l)

Source: [DealElectric — full comparison and pricing](https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv)

## Best alternatives

<box gap={3}>
  <row align="start" gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO portable power station" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="100px"/>
    <box flex="1">
      **Best budget option: Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO**

      $676.16 · 2,048Wh · 2,400W · 51 lb

      Saves roughly $220 versus the BLUETTI, with a TT-30 outlet and expansion capability.

      [RV ranking](https://www.gearranking.com/power-stations/rv/)
    </box>
  </row>
  <divider/>
  <row align="start" gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="OUPES Mega 2 Pro 2048Wh portable power station" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="100px"/>
    <box flex="1">
      **Best value alternative: OUPES Mega 2 Pro**

      $699 · 2,048Wh · 2,500W · 48.8 lb

      Slightly higher AC output and lighter than the BLUETTI, with an RV outlet and substantial expansion potential.

      [RV ranking](https://www.gearranking.com/power-stations/rv/)
    </box>
  </row>
  <divider/>
  <row align="start" gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 portable power station" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="100px"/>
    <box flex="1">
      **Best lightweight option: Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2**

      $899.99 · 41.7 lb

      A compelling choice if weight and portability are more important than maximizing solar charging. The lightest option highlighted in the RV comparison.

      [DealElectric comparison](https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv)
    </box>
  </row>
</box>

## What can 2kWh actually run in your RV?

According to the supplied DealElectric page, a 2,048Wh station delivers roughly **1,700Wh of usable AC energy** after conversion losses.

| RV appliance | Estimated consumption |
|---|---:|
| 12V compressor refrigerator | ~700Wh/day |
| Furnace blower | 300–500Wh/night |
| Lights, phones, water pump, fan | ~200Wh/day |

That translates to approximately **1–1.5 days of basic RV essentials**, or potentially 2–3 days with 200–400W of solar under favorable conditions.

Important: Running rooftop AC on a 2kWh station is generally impractical for extended periods. A microwave is fine for short bursts, but a residential-style electric fridge can consume the entire battery much faster.

Source: [DealElectric runtime and RV power guide](https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv)

---

### Final verdict

- **Best overall RV choice:** BLUETTI AC200L
- **Best value:** Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO
- **Best lighter-weight alternative:** Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2

One caveat: the listed prices are from October 2026 and may change. Also, a TT-30 outlet on a 2,400W inverter does **not** provide the full 30A (3,600W) of campground shore power.

If I were buying specifically for RV boondocking, I'd spend the extra money on the **BLUETTI AC200L**, primarily for its stronger solar charging capability and RV-specific connectivity.

judge.why: The answer picks our BLUETTI AC200L using dealectric.com figures. It gives runtime of 1–1.5 days, or 2–3 days with 200–400 W of solar, and credits dealectric.com. It never covers how to recharge (alternator charger, campground outlet), so the concern is only partly addressed.
judge.concern: How long a 2 kWh station lasts on an RV weekend: about 1.2-1.5 kWh a day (fridge, furnace blower, lights), so about a day and a half on its own and two to three days with 200-400 W of solar, and how to recharge it (solar, an alternator charger, a campground outlet).
